primary.title: Steel tubes, tubulars and other wrought steel fittings - Specification - Part 1: Steel tubes
primary.summary: IS 1239 (Part 1) covers welded and seamless plain-end and screwed-and-socketed mild steel tubes of 6 mm to 150 mm nominal bore, in light, medium and heavy classes, for carrying water, gas, air and steam and for structural use, in black and galvanised (hot-dip zinc coated) finish. It specifies chemical composition, tensile properties, dimensions and tolerances, hydraulic/bend/flattening tests, and the mass and uniformity of the zinc coating for galvanised tubes.

related.title: Steel tubes, tubulars and other wrought steel fittings - Part 2: Steel pipe fittings
related.relation: Companion standard for sockets, bends, tees and other screwed fittings used with the tubes.

related.title: Hot-dip zinc coatings on mild steel tubes
related.relation: Referenced for the zinc coating requirements on galvanised tubes.

related.title: Methods for zinc coating mass and adhesion; general requirements for galvanised steel
related.relation: Test-method and coating standards called up for galvanising checks.

certification.summary: Mild steel tubes to IS 1239 (Part 1) are covered by the Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order administered by the Ministry of Steel. Manufacturers and importers must hold a BIS Scheme I licence and apply the ISI mark with the CM/L number on the tubes before manufacture, import, storage for sale or sale in India.

qco.title: Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order (covers steel tubes to IS 1239 Part 1)
qco.notified: Notified and periodically amended by the Ministry of Steel
qco.enforced: As per the dates in the relevant Steel Products QCO / amendment for IS 1239
qco.gazette: Steel Products QCO, Gazette of India

sources.doc: BIS Product Manual PM/IS 1239 (Part 1) - QCO and marking

applicable.name: Scheme I (ISI Mark Scheme)
applicable.covers: Licence to use the ISI mark on IS 1239 (Part 1) tubes after assessment of the tube mill and testing of samples for chemistry, mechanical properties, dimensions, hydraulic/flattening/bend tests and zinc coating.
applicable.why: Steel tubes under the Steel Products QCO require full ISI-mark certification with a factory Scheme of Inspection and Testing.
applicable.you_receive: A BIS licence with a CM/L number and the right to mark each tube (rolling/stencilling) with the ISI mark; normally valid for 2 years and renewable.

not_applicable.name: Scheme II (CRS)
not_applicable.why: CRS is only for MeitY-notified electronics and IT goods. Steel tubes are covered by Scheme I under the Ministry of Steel QCO.

not_applicable.name: Scheme X
not_applicable.why: Scheme X is for machinery/equipment to a purchaser's specification, not for standard-catalogue steel tubes.

testing.summary: Samples are drawn per class and size group from the mill and tested at a BIS / BIS-recognised laboratory against IS 1239 (Part 1). The mill also runs routine tests under its SIT on each lot.

tests.name: Dimensions, wall thickness and mass per metre vs class
Weld ductility / drift-expanding test (for welded tubes)
Zinc coating mass and uniformity (dip test) for galvanised tubes

sources.doc: BIS Product Manual PM/IS 1239 (Part 1) - tests and SIT

labs.note: Testing needs a laboratory with IS 1239 (Part 1) in its recognised scope and mechanical / chemical / hydraulic test capability for tubes. Confirm scope and validity in the BIS LIMS directory.

entries.name: National Test House (NTH)
entries.scope: Ferrous metals, tubes, mechanical and chemical testing

licensing.summary: Scheme I (ISI mark) licence for IS 1239 (Part 1) tubes is applied for online on Manak Online: apply and pay -> scrutiny -> mill inspection and sample drawal -> independent testing -> grant of licence with the CM/L number.

steps.title: Apply online on Manak Online
steps.detail: Register the firm, file the Scheme I application for IS 1239 (Part 1) with the classes and size range applied for, upload documents, declare the SIT and in-house lab, and pay the fee.

steps.title: Scrutiny of application
steps.detail: BIS verifies the tube-mill process, machinery (mill, galvanising line), and test facilities, and raises queries.
steps.timeline: About 15-30 days after a complete application

steps.title: Factory inspection and sample drawal
steps.detail: A BIS officer inspects the mill, witnesses in-house tests and seals samples covering the size/class groups for independent testing.

steps.title: Independent testing against IS 1239 (Part 1)
steps.detail: Samples tested for chemistry, tensile, dimensions, hydraulic, flattening/bend and zinc coating at a BIS / recognised lab.
steps.timeline: Several weeks depending on lab queue

steps.title: Grant of licence
steps.detail: On a satisfactory inspection and test report, BIS grants the licence and CM/L number for the covered sizes/classes; tubes may then be ISI-marked. Licence normally valid 2 years, renewable.
steps.timeline: Commonly around 4 months from a clean application

documents.summary: Documents for the Scheme I application for IS 1239 (Part 1) tubes. Conditional items depend on the firm and on whether galvanising is done in-house or outsourced.

items.name: Firm / factory establishment proof
items.explanation: Business registration, GST, factory licence or Udyam registration and factory address proof.

items.name: Manufacturing process flow chart and machinery list
items.explanation: Strip slitting, forming, ERW welding, sizing, testing and (if applicable) the hot-dip galvanising line.

items.name: List of test equipment with calibration certificates
items.explanation: Hydraulic test bench, UTM, flattening/bend fixtures, spectrometer or chemical lab, zinc-coating dip-test setup.

items.name: Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT)
items.explanation: Raw-coil, in-process, routine (100% hydraulic) and lot-acceptance test plan with records.

items.name: Raw material (HR/CR coil) test certificates
items.explanation: Mill test certificates for the steel strip/coil used, showing conformance to the grade called up by IS 1239.

items.name: Galvanising subcontract agreement and the subcontractor's process/test details
items.explanation: Needed if hot-dip galvanising is outsourced rather than done in-house.

items.name: Authorised signatory authorisation and ID
items.explanation: Board resolution / partnership authorisation and ID of the signatory.

items.name: Importer: Authorised Indian Representative (AIR) papers
items.explanation: Foreign manufacturers apply through an AIR with appointment letter and undertakings.
